findings.claim: scripts/replay-canary.sh header prose says 'three federation-primitive canaries' (line 4) and 'The three canary branches' (line 14) but the numbered list immediately following (lines 14-24) enumerates FOUR scenarios. The DISPATCH-NOTE acceptance item (iv) asserts the header was 'updated to enumerate the four canaries' — the numbered list was extended correctly but the count noun in the prose was not updated from 'three' to reflect four canary scenarios (two sharing one branch).
findings.evidence: scripts/replay-canary.sh line 4: 'Replays each of the three federation-primitive canaries against the currently-released @main and @v1.* tags'. Lines 14-24 list items 1 (deliberate-violation-pre deny), 2 (same branch post-D-032), 3 (waived-violation), 4 (rule-config-disabled). The CANARIES registry array has 3 entries (deliberate-violation-pre, waived-violation, rule-config-disabled) — consistent with 3 branches — but 4 narrative scenarios. 'Three canary branches' is technically accurate for branch count but contradicts the 4-item numbered list on the same heading line. canary-replay.yml line 2 ('Replays the three SCP federation-primitive canaries') is also stale but is not in this slice's diff.
findings.impact: An operator reading the header derives 'three scenarios' from the prose, then encounters a four-item list; the mismatch creates confusion about whether Canary 2 is in-scope for the weekly cron. Low probability of operational error (the CANARIES array is the source of truth for the cron), but the header is the primary human-readable description for incident responders.
findings.mitigation: Update scripts/replay-canary.sh line 4 from 'three federation-primitive canaries' to 'four federation-primitive canary scenarios (canaries 1 and 2 share a branch)' or equivalent. Optionally update line 14 from 'The three canary branches' to 'The four canary scenarios (three branches — canaries 1 and 2 share canary/deliberate-violation-pre)' for full internal consistency. Also update canary-replay.yml line 2 in a subsequent governance PR (not this slice's diff; not blocking).

findings.claim: The replay-canary.sh registry tuple does not include an expected_disabled_rules_count field, leaving a narrow 'disable still works but observability record dropped' regression class undetectable by the weekly cron.
findings.evidence: scripts/replay-canary.sh line 80 comment: 'name | branch | expected_verdict | expected_findings_count | expected_waivers_count' (5 fields; no disabled_rules field). canary-evidence.md 'Discriminating signature vs Canary 3' section explicitly documents this gap: 'The disabled_rules count is documented as a baseline observation but not used by the registry tuple — extending the tuple to include it is forward-compat (would catch a disable still works but observability record dropped regression class).' DISPATCH-NOTE 'Out of scope' explicitly declines to file a TF for this. A regression where SCP-R-001 deny is suppressed (findings=0, verdict=SUCCESS, waivers=0) but the disabled_rules observability record is dropped (disabled_rules=[]) would pass the registry check and require a human reading the JSON artifact to detect.
findings.impact: Monitoring blind spot for a specific regression class. The primary regression (deny fires when it shouldn't: findings=1, verdict=FAILURE) IS caught. Only the secondary observability regression (deny suppressed correctly but no audit record emitted) is invisible to the cron. Practical risk: low at v1.0.0 single-operator scale; grows with estate cascade (WP-SCP-024).
findings.mitigation: Acceptable as documented forward-compat per DISPATCH-NOTE. If warranted: extend CANARIES tuple to a 6th field expected_disabled_rules_count and add a corresponding jq assertion block after line 127 in replay-canary.sh. Would also catch the case where SCP-R-003 no-manifest-applicable observability record is dropped. Not blocking this slice.
